$comment: Canonical demo addresses for Dryline. Live trio (rehearsed) + four in-the-chamber. See PROPOSAL.md → Demo lineup.

locations.label: Wimberley, TX — Hill Country private well
locations.headlineStory: Trinity Aquifer is dropping ~1.8 ft/yr; the Blanco River goes dry in summer. Will the water last here?
locations.humanScaleHook: The Trinity Aquifer beneath this address is dropping ~1.5 ft/year. Over 20 years that's ~30 ft of water column lost from your well's reach.

locations.label: Taylor, TX — Samsung $17B semiconductor fab
locations.headlineStory: A fab in a town of 16,000 draws several MGD from Lake Granger and the Trinity Aquifer. Who's drinking your aquifer?
locations.humanScaleHook: Samsung Austin Semiconductor's reported NPDES average flow at Taylor is roughly equivalent to the daily water use of 17,000 Texas households (USEPA WaterSense baseline ~110 gal/person/day, 2.5 persons/household). Lake Granger is currently at 67% of conservation capacity vs 78% historical for this date.

locations.label: Fort Stockton, TX — Comanche Springs
locations.headlineStory: Comanche Springs flowed for centuries until 1950s irrigation pumping dried them up. The Belding case cemented rule-of-capture. Live permit fight: Republic Water → El Paso.
locations.humanScaleHook: Comanche Springs flowed continuously for centuries until 1955, when irrigation pumping dried them up. The 1954 Pecos County WCID v. Williams decision cemented Texas's rule of capture — the legal framework that made the dry-up possible.

locations.label: Houston Memorial — Buffalo Bayou
locations.headlineStory: Harvey-zone flood exposure layered against drinking water and Addicks/Barker reservoir release context.

locations.label: Lubbock, TX — Ogallala Aquifer
locations.headlineStory: The canonical American aquifer-depletion story. Decades of decline, cotton irrigation as the named driver.

locations.label: El Paso, TX — Hueco Bolson + KBH desalination
locations.headlineStory: A positive water story — largest inland desalination plant in the U.S., Hueco Bolson management, treaty water from Mexico.

locations.label: San Antonio — Edwards Aquifer recharge zone
locations.headlineStory: Most-regulated aquifer in Texas. EAA permit caps, J-17 monitoring well, growth pressure.
